analysis: Package.swift: adds ProviderBuildEnvironment target (head 73-77) that now owns the DARKBLOOM_ENV_DEV define via buildEnvironmentSwiftSettings. ProviderCore (head 169) loses its swiftSettings and no longer receives the define directly. ProviderAppAttest, ProviderCoreFoundation and ProviderCore now depend on ProviderBuildEnvironment. ProviderBuildEnvironment's source is not supplied. Any remaining `#if DARKBLOOM_ENV_DEV` in ProviderCore, or in other modules that previously inherited the define, would silently compile as prod. That would affect coordinator URL, CDN and install identity selection, and A-008 token issuer binding. The next pass should grep for such conditionals and confirm the BuildEnvironment re-export works, covering dev/prod App Attest identity separation (TB-011, A-015/A-016) and any key or keychain label separation. No security regression is evident in the visible manifest. FanDaemon.swift (TB-010, T-044/T-046/T-047, A-014): the single providerLease is replaced by per-session providerLeases [UUID: TimeInterval]. Expired entries are pruned on renew. Leases are cleared on sleep, wake, shutdown and emergencyRestore. Release and invalidation restore Auto only when no live lease remains. Leases are added only via renewLease, which still checks effectiveEnabled, protocol version and powerSuspended. The map is bounded by the number of XPC sessions and pruned on renew. Residual: with two concurrent sessions, a stuck or malicious second peer that keeps renewing now keeps manual fan control on after the first provider stops. Previously its lease replaced the first one, so this is no worse than before. Whether the XPC peer validation in FanXPCService, which is not changed here, admits dev and prod provider identities needs confirming (T-044). FanXPCService.swift: the fallback encoding-failure JSON now interpolates FanIPC constants instead of hard-coded 1/1. This is benign. No findings.
